strings.name: Robert Kahn
strings.summary: Robert Kahn extended packet-network research to internetworking and worked with Vint Cerf on the architecture that became TCP/IP. He contributed to ARPANET at BBN, led Internet research at DARPA, and founded CNRI to advance information infrastructure and digital object architecture. The Internet was a collective achievement; Kahn’s contributions centered on open interconnection and research leadership.

strings.influence.rationale: Co-designed TCP/IP and advanced Internet architecture, establishing important foundations for connecting heterogeneous networks.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Foundations of internetworking

strings.timeline.event-5.title: Founded CNRI

strings.timeline.event-6.title: Internetworking paper
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Published with Cerf on interconnecting packet networks, a foundation of TCP/IP.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Joined DARPA

strings.timeline.event-9.title: Princeton doctorate
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Completed an electrical engineering PhD, followed by work at Bell Labs and MIT.
